narrative:
The model predicts you have a 10% chance of failing your final year. While this is a low probability, the school has decided this risk is high enough that you are required to take remedial courses to strengthen your performance.

The prediction that you might fail is driven primarily by three key aspects of your background. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually works against you in the model's view compared to many students who passed. The second strongest influence is your strong desire to pursue higher education, which should normally help but in your specific combination of circumstances pulled the prediction slightly toward risk. The third notable factor is your mother's education level, which is at 5th to 9th grade. This is lower than the education level of mothers of most students who successfully passed.

Taken together, these elements led the model to recommend extra support. To improve, you should focus on maintaining consistent study habits beyond your current 2 to 5 hours per week, minimize your 10 absences (more than double the average of students who passed), and make full use of the remedial courses to close any small gaps before final exams. This extra preparation can help turn your 10% risk into a clear pass. (218 words)
